extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing examiner guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and drafting Office actions, citing references, and responding to applicant arguments during patent examination at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not abbreviate titles of books and periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated because an abbreviation will not be sufficient to identify the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are to be cited so that anyone reading a patent may identify and retrieve the publications cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: References must permit identification and retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic information provided must be at least enough to identify the publication: author, title and date for books; for periodicals at least the title of the periodical, the volume number, date, and pages should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal citations may be made ONLY IF the complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include document identification and class/subclass on PTO-892 for NPL with document ID
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (S00840001) Winslow, C.E.A. Fresh Air and Ventilation N.Y., E.P. Dutton, 1926, p. 97-112, TH 7653, W5, 315/22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain photocopy of original publications located outside the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office, the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed, if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow WIPO ST.14 format for electronic document citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The format for the citation of an electronic document is as similar as possible to the format used for paper documents of the same type, but with the addition of specific information where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (A) the type of electronic medium in square brackets after the title (e.g., [online], [CD-ROM]); (B) the date when the document was retrieved in square brackets, with four-digit year; (C) identification of the source using 'Retrieved from' and address; (D) specific passages indicated if pagination or equivalent exists or by first/last words of passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain office copies of electronic documents that may become unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Office copies of an electronic document must be retained if the same document may not be available for retrieval in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important for Internet and online database sources. If an electronic document is also available in paper form it does not need to be identified as electronic unless desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete citation examples for electronic sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations for electronic sources should follow provided examples covering databases, Internet pages, bulletin boards, email, CD-ROMs, and datasheets, showing retrieval statements, accession numbers, and URLs where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the illustrated examples (Examples 1–14) as templates for various electronic citation types (entire works, parts, serials, bulletin boards, email, CD-ROM products, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When using declassified material as references, consider both the printing date and the publication (release) date; the date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication for anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The printing date may be prima facie evidence of prior knowledge under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) even if classified at that time, but such printing date may be antedated by affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for incorrect citation of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an error in citation of a reference is brought to the attention of the Office by applicant, a letter correcting the error, together with a correct copy of the reference, is sent to applicant. Where the error is discovered by the examiner, applicant is also notified and the period for reply restarted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should correct the error, in ink, in the paper in which the error appears, place initials on the margin, and note the paper number of the action in which citation has been correctly given. See MPEP § 710.06. Form paragraphs 7.81–7.83 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form paragraphs for citation corrections and supplying copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.81–7.83 are available for restarting reply periods, correcting reference citations, and indicating copies supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.81 restarts the reply period and must be followed by 7.82/7.83; ¶7.82 states the correct citation and every correction MUST be reflected on a corrected or new PTO-892; ¶7.82.01 lists copies furnished; ¶7.83 encloses a copy of an Office action or explains what is enclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle incorrect foreign patent citations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a FOREIGN patent is incorrectly cited (wrong or omitted country), the General Reference Branch of the Scientific and Technical Library may assist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date and number of the patent are often sufficient to determine the correct country which granted the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of decisions, orders, memorandums, and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing court decisions, the USPQ citation should be given and, when convenient, the U.S., CCPA or Federal Reporter citation should also be provided; avoid citing manuscript decisions not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A federal district court decision reversed on appeal cannot be cited as authority. For manuscript decisions available to the public but unpublished, give tribunal and complete identifying data. Decisions found only in patent files should be cited only when there is no published decision on the same point. When citing Director's orders/notices/memoranda not yet in the manual, give title and date and other locating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects) the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters of form need not be raised by the examiner until a claim is found allowable. (See 37 CFR 1.104.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete action on formal matters in first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms listing informalities (PTO-948 and PTO-152) should be used and mailed with the examiner's first action; any additional formal requirements desired should be included in the first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms comprise an original for the file and a copy to be mailed to applicant; for IFW processing see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: When indicating allowable subject matter, require compliance or traversal of formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When any formal requirement is made in an examiner's action that indicates allowable subject matter, the action should call attention to 37 CFR 1.111(b) and state that a complete reply must either comply with all formal requirements or specifically traverse each requirement not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.43.03 (Allowable Subject Matter, Formal Requirements Outstanding) would be appropriate when changes (e.g., drawing corrections) must be made prior to allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid expressing personal opinions about patentable merit
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should not express in the record the opinion that the application is, or appears to be, devoid of patentable subject matter or express doubts as to the allowability of allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything of a personal nature must be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify allowable claims and suggest amendments in first merits action
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the first Office action on the merits, the examiner should identify any claims judged to be allowable and/or suggest ways in which rejected claims may be amended to make them allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner does not do this, applicant may reasonably infer there are no allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and format required when rejecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is refused for any reason relating to the merits it should be 'rejected' and the ground of rejection fully and clearly stated, and the word 'reject' must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should designate the statutory basis by express reference to a section of 35 U.S.C. in the opening sentence of each ground of rejection; explain why rejected as broader than enabling disclosure, point out where indefiniteness resides, or specify elements lacking for incompleteness. Avoid omnibus rejections and grouping claim pluralities unless equally applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note all outstanding requirements in subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all requirements outstanding against the application; every point in the prior action still applicable must be repeated or referred to to prevent implied waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requirements include information under 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP § 704.10; determine whether satisfied by negative reply under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3). As soon as allowable subject matter is found, correction of all informalities then present should be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all material traversed and respond to applicant's arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a complete application file history and enhance clarity, an examiner must provide clear explanations of all actions taken and answer the substance of applicant's arguments when they are traversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's arguments are persuasive and prior rejection is withdrawn, the examiner must state reasons and refer specifically to the pages/lines of applicant's remarks forming the basis for withdrawal. If withdrawal results in allowance, reasons may be included in a reasons-for-allowance statement. If withdrawal leads to a new ground, use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.38.02). When arguments are not persuasive use form paragraphs 7.37–7.37.13; when moot due to new grounds use 7.38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Age of Reference(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Age of the references is not impressive absent a showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem notwithstanding its presumed knowledge of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use In re Wright (569 F.2d 1124) as authority; this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Bodily Incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is not whether the features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into the structure of the primary reference; rather, the test is what the combined teachings of the references would have suggested to those of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Keller; in bracket insert brief restatement of applicant's argument regarding bodily incorporation. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Hindsight Reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Although any judgment on obviousness is in a sense a reconstruction based on hindsight, it is proper so long as it accounts only for knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time and does not include knowledge gleaned only from the applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re McLaughlin. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: No Suggestion To Combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness can be established by combining or modifying teachings of the prior art where there is some teaching, suggestion, or motivation to do so found either in the references themselves or in knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket explain where the motivation is found (in references or general knowledge). See In re Fine and In re Jones. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Nonanalogous Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must either be in the field of applicant's endeavor or, if not, then be reasonably pertinent to the particular problem with which the applicant was concerned to be relied upon for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the alleged nonanalogous reference is, in fact, analogous. See In re Oetiker. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Number of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a large number of references in a rejection does not, without more, weigh against the obviousness of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Gorman. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Applicant Obtains Result Not Contemplated by Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A new advantage which would flow naturally from following the suggestion of the prior art cannot be the basis for patentability when the differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Obiaya. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Limitations Which Are Not Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Features upon which applicant relies but which are not recited in the rejected claims cannot be relied upon; limitations from the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the non-claimed features applicant relies on. See In re Van Geuns. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of the intended use of the claimed invention must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art in order to patentably distinguish the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art structure is capable of performing the intended use, then it meets the claim. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Limitation(s) in Preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble is generally not accorded patentable weight where it merely recites the purpose of a process or the intended use of a structure and where the body of the claim can stand alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Hirao and Kropa v. Robie. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: General Allegation of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's general allegations that the claims define a patentable invention are insufficient under 37 CFR 1.111(b); arguments must specifically point out how claim language patentably distinguishes over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Novelty Not Clearly Pointed Out
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that do not clearly point out the patentable novelty in view of the cited art and do not show how amendments avoid such references fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Against References Individually
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where the rejections are based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Keller and In re Merck. Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid piecemeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided; the examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major technical rejections (e.g., lack of disclosure, lack of enablement, serious indefiniteness) should be applied where appropriate with full development of reasons. Do not routinely make secondary rejections when prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention. Situations where limiting action on claims may be appropriate include: (A) application too informal for complete action; (B) undue multiplicity of claims and no successful telephone election; (C) misjoinder of inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When inaccuracies in an amendment are found, the examiner should notify as provided (see MPEP § 714.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to MPEP § 714.23 for detailed handling; this is a requirement to notify applicants of inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in each Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: In every Office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given; each action should include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PTO-326 'Office Action Summary'. Keep the Index of Claims up to date as set forth in MPEP § 719.04. Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated per MPEP § 821–821.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: State when claims are allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are allowable, the examiner should state that the claims are allowable in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate status clearly (see heading 'State When Claims Are Allowable [R-2]'). Further procedural detail appears elsewhere in the MPEP.
